quote: The sum of the whole matter is this: write quickly and you will never write well, write well and you will soon write quickly.
source: Quintilian, Institutio Oratoria, X.3.10 (trans. H. E. Butler, 1922)

evidence.where: Bill Thayer’s LacusCurtius transcription of the Loeb edition, Book X chapter 3, fetched this run; the sentence is there word for word at section 10, between the ‘well-ordered household’ sentence and ‘curb the horses’.
evidence.edition: The Institutio Oratoria of Quintilian, trans. H. E. Butler, Loeb Classical Library, vol. IV (1922)

reason: Located verbatim in Butler’s Loeb text at the section named. A treatise on the training of a writer, not a speech, so in scope; not shipped, not banned, Quintilian unused. The Loeb page number is dropped from the source because it was not seen.
